summary: Radar, 2026-11-16. ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) and the FDA's class-wide NAION label change (Nov 9) are the two main news drivers. Neither gives us a fresh randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide. I checked the EloraTZP figures being repeated at ObesityWeek (23.3% vs 14.8% for tirzepatide alone, 48 weeks, adults with type 2 diabetes plus overweight or obesity). They are the same EASD data from Sept 30, so they are not new and are not a 48-hour trigger. The new randomized tirzepatide result is SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (JAMA, Nov 15: BMI −18.5% vs +0.5% on placebo at 72 weeks). It suits a calm news hook, but our audience is adults, so it ranks mid. The biggest openings line up with the playbook's broad, searched questions. (1) Months 2–6 / what to expect, which now has a fresh hook: Medscape (Nov 15) on whether early weight loss predicts the 1-year result, backed by the SURMOUNT post hoc numbers (people with ≥5% loss at 8 weeks averaged 23.3% at 72 weeks, vs 14.6% for the rest). (2) Keeping results after stopping, with news coverage still growing: Medscape's 'exit strategy' piece, the Fox 'rebound risks' story and Yahoo's 'stopping may raise stroke risk'. (3) The Thanksgiving table (Prevention, Nov 15), with Shorts starting Nov 18. (4) The NAION label change, which is peaking but fits the label-change format: FDA 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years. Evergreen felt-symptom and device searches (injection sites per the IFU, hair loss, nausea, Mounjaro vs Zepbound, how much weight loss in the trials) stay in the mix as required. I rejected the pricing, CVS, compounded and peptide-supplier stories, the black-market injection story, the dosing-change survey, the observational switching study, the conflicting observational semaglutide-vs-tirzepatide heart studies, and the DJ Khaled campaign.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) months 2–6: what to expect, with the new early-response hook (in SURMOUNT post hoc data, people who lost ≥5% by week 8 averaged 23.3% at 72 weeks, vs 14.6% for the rest)
candidates.angle: A sequel to First Month. It walks month by month through what the label and the SURMOUNT-1 average curve show, then answers the question people worry about most: 'Am I a slow responder?' Frame it honestly: early response predicts the average result, not destiny. Explain what to bring up with your prescriber, and say clearly that you should never change your dose yourself. Watch next: How Long. Add it to the 'Your First Months on Tirzepatide' playlist.

Make clear that any decision about stopping happens with your prescriber. Watch next: Stopping, which links on to Keeping Results.

Show the real scale of the risk (a few extra cases per 100,000 people a year), what NAION is, which sudden vision changes mean get urgent care, and that you should keep taking the medicine and ask your prescriber rather than stopping on your own. It can also be a chapter in 'Serious Risks: How Rare?'.
